summary.text: Pat Proctor is the Republican nominee for Kansas Secretary of State. A retired U.S. Army colonel and restaurant owner, he has represented Kansas House District 41 since 2021 and chairs the House Elections Committee.

paragraphs.text: Proctor enlisted in the Army as a private in 1989 and served until 2019, retiring as a colonel, with combat tours in Iraq and Afghanistan.
He earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Purdue University in 1994, three military-related master's degrees, and a doctorate in history from Kansas State University in 2014.
In 1998 he founded ProSIM Company, which develops military simulation games.
After his doctorate he taught at Benedictine College and then in the Homeland Security program at Wichita State University.
He and his wife own restaurants in Leavenworth and Manhattan.
Proctor was first elected to the Kansas House in 2020, defeating Mike Griswold 53 percent to 47 percent, and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.
He chairs the House Elections Committee and the Joint Committee on Kansas Security.

His campaign says he carried the Citizens-Only Voting amendment and the SAVE Kansas Act, and he championed a law ending the three-day grace period for mail-in ballots, which the Kansas Court of Appeals later reinstated; Democrats have said his election bills would suppress their voters.
He advanced from the Republican primary on August 4, 2026.
